reasons: Classification is correct: the cap basis (greater of $100k or 12 months' charges) and mutuality (Sections 9.1/9.2 drafted symmetrically) meet the fallback, but the fallback expressly requires carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct — here only indemnity (and bodily injury/property damage) sits outside the cap, and Section 6 affirmatively pulls confidentiality of hosting-environment information inside Sections 9/10. That is a material shortfall on a named fallback term, not a minor sub-element, so deviation is appropriate rather than over-flagging.

Redline is minimal and actionable: a single mutual 'Excluded Claims' sentence added as new Section 9.3 that expressly overrides the final sentence of Section 6, leaving the acceptable cap language untouched — exactly the 'add one carve-out sentence' approach the redline guidance prescribes.

The failed deterministic check ('cap references 12 months of fees or a fixed floor') is a false signal here: the existing cap already satisfies the fallback basis, so no edit to the cap sentence was needed and none was made.

Comment is accurate, correctly cites the playbook position (indemnities/confidentiality outside the cap, mutual), acknowledges the cap works for us, and observes the one-sided data-loss exclusion in 9.1(c)(2) as a note rather than a second flag; tone and prefix conform.
Edit does not disadvantage our party beyond the playbook's own mutuality requirement, and no duplicate flagging of the consequential-damages exclusion (Section 10) occurs.
